articles.full_text:
ग्रीष्म ऋतु की शुरुआत से लेकर अब तक यूरोप में भीषण गर्मी के कारण लगभग 20,000 मौतें दर्ज की गई हैं। अत्यधिक गर्मी सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य के लिए, विशेषकर बुजुर्गों के लिए, एक गंभीर खतरा बनती जा रही है।
यूरोप बुजुर्गों को भीषण गर्मी से बचाने के लिए काम कर रहा है।
VTV.vn - कई यूरोपीय देश बुजुर्गों को अत्यधिक गर्मी के गंभीर प्रभावों से बचाने के लिए उपाय लागू कर रहे हैं।
इस स्थिति के जवाब में, कई यूरोपीय देश चरम मौसम के प्रभाव को कम करने के लिए तत्काल उपाय लागू कर रहे हैं।
यूरोप में भीषण गर्मी के दिनों में, स्विट्जरलैंड के जिनेवा में स्थित सिनेमाघर न केवल मनोरंजन का स्थान होते हैं, बल्कि सैकड़ों बुजुर्ग लोगों के लिए गर्मी से राहत पाने का एक आश्रय स्थल भी होते हैं।
65 वर्ष और उससे अधिक आयु के सभी नागरिकों को शाम 7 बजे से पहले प्रमुख सिनेमाघरों में निःशुल्क प्रवेश दिया जाता है। सिनेमाघरों के अंदर तापमान आरामदायक स्तर पर बनाए रखा जाता है, जिससे वरिष्ठ नागरिकों को बाहर की भीषण गर्मी से राहत मिलती है।
3 अगस्त, 2026 को इंग्लैंड के लंदन स्थित ग्रीन पार्क में लोग सूखी घास पर बैठे हैं। (फोटो: एपी)
82 वर्षीय डेनियल गिलीरॉन ने बताया, “यह बहुत बढ़िया है क्योंकि इससे हमें घर से बाहर निकलने, ठंडे, आरामदायक, वातानुकूलित सिनेमाघर में जाने और अच्छा समय बिताने का मौका मिलता है। मैं अब अकेला रहता हूँ क्योंकि मेरी पत्नी का निधन हो चुका है और मैं बहुत अकेला महसूस करता हूँ। फिल्में देखने से मुझे लोगों से मिलने और अच्छी फिल्म का आनंद लेने में मदद मिलती है।”
इस बीच, इटली में सामाजिक संगठनों ने बुजुर्गों की सुरक्षा के लिए कई व्यावहारिक उपाय लागू किए हैं। इन संगठनों के कर्मचारी घर-घर जाकर उनकी देखभाल करते हैं, भोजन उपलब्ध कराते हैं और अकेले रहने वाले बुजुर्गों के स्वास्थ्य पर कड़ी निगरानी रखते हैं।
व्यायाम कक्षाओं को भी खुले में आयोजित होने वाले स्थानों से हटाकर वातानुकूलित सुविधाओं में स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया है, और वरिष्ठ नागरिकों को सुरक्षित रूप से व्यायाम करने में मदद करने और खराब मौसम के प्रभाव को कम करने के लिए प्रशिक्षण समय को समायोजित किया गया है।
जिम्नास्टिक कोच रीटा लोपेज़ ने कहा, "गर्म मौसम अक्सर बुजुर्ग लोगों को व्यायाम करने से हतोत्साहित करता है। इसीलिए हमने अपने वर्कआउट का समय दिन के अन्य समयों के बजाय सुबह के लिए निर्धारित किया है।"
प्रत्यक्ष सामुदायिक सहायता के अलावा, कई यूरोपीय देशों ने प्रारंभिक चेतावनी प्रणाली का निर्माण किया है, सार्वजनिक ताप आश्रय खोले हैं और अपने स्वास्थ्य सेवा क्षेत्रों की प्रतिक्रिया क्षमता को बढ़ाया है।

Typhoon Dolphin is expected to enter the East China Sea on Saturday and intensify rainfall in western regions over the weekend as the typhoon’s outer circulation sweeps across the sea north of Taiwan, independent meteorologist Daniel Wu (吳德榮) said today.
The eastern coast should prepare for extreme heat caused by downslope winds over the weekend, while southwesterly winds from Monday would bring localized heavy rain to the southwest, he said.
Photo courtesy of the Central Weather Administration
As Typhoon Dolphin’s outer bands move past northern Taiwan over the next couple of days, northern, central and southern areas would experience showers tomorrow, he said.
Rainfall over the weekend would lead to slightly cooler weather, though eastern Taiwan could experience extreme high temperatures, he said, adding that strong wind is expected across the country.
From Monday to Wednesday next week, as the typhoon moves away, Taiwan would be dominated by southwesterly winds, bringing localized showers, thunderstorms and heavy rain to the southwest, he said.
Other areas would remain sunny and hot and extreme heat is expected in northern and southeastern Taiwan, while afternoon thunderstorms are likely north of central Taiwan due to atmospheric instability, he said.
Between Thursday and Saturday next week, southwesterly winds would weaken, but moisture would remain high, with early morning rain expected in the southwest and afternoon showers in mountainous areas, he said.
Typhoon Dolphin remains a large moderate typhoon moving westward and is projected to pass near Japan's Ryukyu Islands before entering the southern portion of the East China Sea on Saturday, he said.
The angle of its northward turn is critical to how it affects Taiwan and uncertainty surrounding its exact trajectory is increasing, he added.
Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Kujira is forming off the western coast of Luzon in the Philippines and is expected to make landfall there before weakening into a tropical depression, he said.
Tropical Storm Chan-hom is moving northwest toward waters east of Japan, meaning no conditions exist that would enable the three storms to interact, he added.
Citing the latest ensemble simulations from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Wu said that predicted paths for Typhoon Dolphin diverge starting on Saturday, depending on how quickly a high-pressure system to the north weakens.
If the storm tracks further west toward China before turning back, its impact on Taiwan would be more severe, but if it turns north immediately upon entering the East China Sea, the effect would be minimal, he said.
Winds near Taiwan shifted northeast today, bringing occasional localized short showers to windward northern areas, while afternoon thunderstorms are expected in central and southern mountainous areas, extending to some plains, although most of Taiwan remains sunny and hot, he said.

South Korea’s professional baseball league canceled all games scheduled for yesterday and today amid a record-setting heat wave that has sent spectators to hospitals.
The country has been sweltering in a streak of searing weather — new all-time highs were set three times over the past week alone, peaking at 42.5°C on Sunday.
The KBO’s announcement came a day after South Korean President Lee Jae-myung asked authorities to treat the heat wave “as a national disaster” and “make every effort to swiftly implement necessary measures” to protect lives.
Photo: Reuters
The east and west regions of Seoul yesterday were under the highest-level heat alert, issued when the heat index is forecast to reach 38°C or temperatures are expected to climb to 39°C or higher.
“We have decided to call off all games on Aug. 5 and 6 until comprehensive safety measures are established,” the KBO said in a statement, citing risks to players and fans as extreme temperatures persist.
According to local reports, 10 games scheduled for yesterday and today across the country were canceled.
The league said it would convene an emergency executive committee meeting with club officials and representatives of the players’ association to discuss additional safety measures.
The KBO canceled two games on Tuesday at Seoul’s Jamsil Stadium and the southwestern city of Gwangju after multiple spectators collapsed due to the heat.
During Tuesday’s game between the SSG Landers and LG Twins in Incheon, a male spectator collapsed from a suspected heat-related illness, prompting a nine-minute suspension before he was taken to a hospital by ambulance, an SSG official said.
Twenty-five spectators were treated for heat-related illnesses during the game, the SSG Landers said.

Rabat – Morocco’s General Directorate of Meteorology (DGM) has issued an updated orange-level weather alert warning of a heatwave, thunderstorms, hail, and strong winds in several parts of the country from Wednesday through Friday.
Temperatures are expected to range between 44 and 47 degrees Celsius from Wednesday to Friday in the provinces and prefectures of Errachidia, Taroudant, Zagora, Tata, Assa-Zag, Smara, Boujdour, Oued Ed-Dahab, and Aousserd.
The heatwave is also expected to affect Essaouira on Wednesday, with temperatures ranging between 39 and 42 degrees Celsius.
The DGM also warned of thunderstorms bringing between 20 and 35 millimeters of rainfall, along with hail and strong wind gusts, in several regions on Wednesday.
The affected areas include Midelt, Boulemane, Beni Mellal, Azilal, Al Haouz, Tinghir, Taroudant, Ouarzazate, and Zagora.
The thunderstorms are expected to begin at 1 p.m. and continue until 11 p.m. on Wednesday.
The weather authority urged residents in the affected areas to remain cautious and follow official weather updates.
Morocco experienced high temperatures in recent weeks, with many residents seeking relief from the heat by heading to beaches, swimming pools, and other cooler areas.
Coastal cities, especially Agadir, have seen large crowds during the summer season as families and young people travel to the seaside to escape the intense heat affecting inland regions.
Beaches have become particularly busy during weekends, while many Moroccans have also chosen to travel at night or spend more time indoors during the hottest hours of the day.

articles.title: South Korea: Heat-related death toll rises to 21 amid serious heat wave - Eastern Mirror

articles.full_text:
A total of 21 people have died from heat-related illnesses in South Korea so far this year as the country grapples with intense heat, health authorities said Wednesday.
SEOUL — A total of 21 people have died from heat-related illnesses in South Korea so far this year as the country grapples with intense heat, health authorities said Wednesday.
A total of 2,441 patients have visited emergency rooms for heat-related conditions as of Tuesday since mid-May, when authorities launched the heat-related illness surveillance system, according to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.
Although fewer people suffered heat-related illnesses this year than during the same period last year, more people died this year, with the death toll surpassing last year's total of 20, Yonhap News Agency reported.
One of the latest fatalities was a 60-year-old man, who was working outside on a farm in the county of Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, on Tuesday.
Among the patients reported this year, heat exhaustion accounted for 61.7 per cent, followed by heat stroke at 16.8 per cent and heat cramps at 11.5 per cent.

The state weather agency issued additional serious heat wave warnings for the greater Seoul area earlier in the day, placing 43 per cent of the region under the highest alert level.
Meanwhile, temperatures for July this year in South Korea were the third highest on record at an average of 26.8 C nationwide, the state weather agency said Wednesday.
The highest on record was 27.7 C in 1994, followed by 27.1 C last year, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA), which tracks records using 1973 as the base year.
The number of tropical nights when the lowest temperature was 25 C or above came to an average of 9.7 days nationwide, setting a new record.
The previous mark had been 8.8 days in July 2024, followed by 8.5 days in July 1994, the KMA said.
Also in July this year, a heat wave advisory was issued on an average of 8.9 days nationwide, as the daily maximum temperature climbed to 33 C or higher.
The heat was most intense in the southeastern region, with the advisory triggered on 22 days in Daegu, 21 days in Gumi and 20 days in Miryang. By contrast, the central region saw far fewer days under heat wave advisories, with only two in Seoul.
Nationwide precipitation only came to 220.2 millimetres, or 72.3 per cent of the average July rainfall of 296.5 mm, according to the KMA.
Drought conditions were most severe in the southeastern South Gyeongsang Province, which received 68 mm of rainfall last month, or 21.9 per cent of the average July precipitation of 304.7 mm.

UK weather maps show possible hottest day of year as 8 counties hit 37C or more
Temperatures in some parts of the UK could surge past 37C once more next week, as Met Office weather forecasters say conditions may turn ‘very warm or hot’ once again
Weather forecasting models show the UK could see the hottest day of the year so far next week.
The current temperature record for 2026 stands at 37.7C, which came on June 26 in Lingwood, Norfolk. However, temperatures could rise past 37C again next week, data suggests.
The GFS weather model shows maximum temperatures reaching 34C on Wednesday next week in southern England, in an area stretching from Gloucestershire to Surrey. South Wales could hit 31C, while the Midlands may rise as high as 33C.
Highs of 36C are possible quite widely across western and southern England on Thursday next week, the model shows, with temperatures climbing to 33C in areas as far north as Yorkshire, and 28C in southern parts of Scotland.
Western England and south-east England could then see highs of at least 37C on Friday next week. The model shows 36C is possible quite widely across central England and southern areas.
For Saturday next week, maps show potential highs of 36C in East Anglia, 33C in Yorkshire, 36C in the south-east, and 33-34C in the Midlands. This hot spell would constitute another official heatwave across the four days.
Temperature anomaly maps for next week show the UK shaded in areas of deep red. This indicates where temperatures will rise well above the seasonal average.
In total, the GFS model suggests temperatures may reach 37C or more in eight counties next week. They are all in England.
UK counties facing 37C next week
Met Office weather forecast
The Met Office says conditions could potentially turn ‘very warm or hot’ again later this month. However, there is also the potential for some ‘thundery interludes’.
The Met Office forecast for August 9 to 18 states: “Further into August, high pressure may become more dominant towards the north or northwest of the UK, with lower pressure to the south or east.
“This means there is a greater chance of frontal systems or thundery interludes to affect southern and eastern areas in comparison to recent weeks, though rainfall amounts could be quite variable with some areas still seeing relatively little.
“For the most part, temperatures look to remain above average, especially in the south, and perhaps turning very warm or hot.”

Patna: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Patna, has issued an orange alert for most parts of Bihar, forecasting heavy rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds over the next three days, even as recent showers have brought respite from heat and humidity across the state.
Despite the recent wet spell, the state continues to face a 38% monsoon rainfall deficit, with Patna recording a 51% shortfall.
According to IMD Patna, favourable conditions created by two cyclonic circulations the monsoon trough passing through Bihar are likely to trigger widespread rainfall across the state over the next four days.
Meteorologist
Kumar Gaurav said south Bihar districts, including Gaya, Nawada and Arwal, could receive higher rainfall than other parts of the state.
The IMD bulletin issued on Wednesday said maximum temperatures are likely to dip by 2-3 degrees Celsius over the next two days before rising by 2-4 degrees Celsius during the following four days.
Gaurav said the prevailing overcast conditions were typical of the monsoon season. “Low clouds form due to high humidity and bring rainfall. These moving dark clouds generally do not result in intense thunderstorms or lightning activity,” he said.
The IMD has issued an orange alert for Thursday and Friday for south-west and south-central Bihar, warning of thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph. Heavy rainfall is likely in Buxar, Aurangabad, Gaya and Rohtas districts, while East Champaran, Kishanganj and Sitamarhi may experience very heavy rainfall.
A yellow alert has also been issued for several districts, including Araria, Katihar and Siwan. However, districts such as Siwan, Supaul and Lakhisarai no longer show a rainfall deficit following recent showers.
Gaurav said temperatures could rise again once skies clear. While humidity levels may decline, the increase in temperature could make weather conditions uncomfortable for residents.

Thiruvananthapuram: Heavy rains continued to lash several parts of Kerala on Wednesday, causing widespread waterlogging and inundation of roads. More relief camps were opened, and residents of low-lying areas were evacuated, authorities said.
The southern districts of Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha and Kottayam continued to bear the brunt of the rain fury, with incessant showers and overcast skies disrupting normal life.
The elderly, women and children were seen wading through knee-deep water in several inundated areas of these districts.
As floodwaters remained in many low-lying areas and several houses continued to be waterlogged, more residents were shifted to relief camps.
Authorities said additional camps had been opened to accommodate those evacuated as heavy rain persisted.
Several parts of the northern districts, including high-range areas of Kozhikode and Kannur, also received widespread rainfall.
The India Meteorological Department issued an 'orange alert' for five districts in Kerala, warning of very heavy rainfall, while the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services cautioned about the possibility of high waves and sea incursion along parts of the state's southern coast.
The IMD issued an 'orange alert' for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
On Thursday, the alert will remain in force for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
For Friday, an 'orange alert' has been issued for Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts, the IMD said.
An 'orange alert' indicates the likelihood of very heavy rainfall ranging from 115 mm to 204 mm.
According to the weather agency, isolated places in the state are likely to receive heavy rainfall, while very heavy rainfall is expected at isolated locations on August 6 and 7.
INCOIS issued a warning about the 'kallakkadal' phenomenon, a sudden swell of the sea that can lead to rough waves and coastal flooding.
The warning covers the coastal stretch from Kappil to Pozhiyoor in Thiruvananthapuram district, Alappad to Edava in Kollam district, and Chellanam to Azhikkal Jetty in Alappuzha district.
INCOIS warned of high waves measuring 1.2 metres to 1.6 metres along the Kanyakumari coast until 2.30 pm on Thursday, with the possibility of sea incursion.
Authorities advised fishermen, coastal residents and the public to remain vigilant and avoid venturing into vulnerable coastal areas during the warning period.
In view of the alerts, the Kerala Disaster Management Authority advised fishermen and coastal residents to remain vigilant, avoid beaches and tourism-related activities until the INCOIS warning is withdrawn, and exercise caution against possible coastal erosion.
As rains continued, the KSDMA urged people living in landslide, mudslide and flash flood-prone hilly regions to move to safer locations during daytime.
It also advised residents of flood-prone low-lying areas to shift to relief camps after assessing the local situation.
People were advised against entering rivers and other water bodies for bathing, fishing or any other purpose during the heavy rains.
The authority urged the public to avoid non-essential travel during intense rainfall and refrain from visiting waterfalls, reservoirs and hilly tourist destinations until the weather warning is withdrawn.
It advised motorists to exercise caution while travelling along roads near water bodies and stretches undergoing repair work, citing the increased risk of accidents during heavy rain.
People were advised against gathering on bridges over rivers or water bodies for sightseeing or taking selfies, while night travel to hilly regions should be avoided.
The authority warned of accidents caused by uprooted trees and damaged electric posts due to strong winds.
Educational institutions in 10 rain-affected districts, including Idukki and Kottayam, remained closed on Wednesday due to the heavy rainfall.

articles.title: Egypt eases industrial land transfer rules, activity changes, and relief measures for delayed projects - Dailynewsegypt
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
Egypt’s Minister of Industry, Khaled Hashem, has issued Ministerial Decree No. 171 of 2026, amending provisions of Decree No. 107 of 2026 to introduce a new package of incentives aimed at removing obstacles facing serious industrial investors, accelerating production, and improving the management of industrial land.
The amendments abolish the previous requirement for factories to operate for three years before owners could transfer ownership or for one year before leasing industrial land.
Instead, investors will only be required to demonstrate the seriousness of their projects by obtaining an operating licence and an industrial registration certificate, paying the full price of the land, and commencing production before transferring ownership, assigning rights, or leasing industrial land.
The move follows the minister’s recent announcement suspending the implementation of Ministerial Decree No. 107 from mid-August until the end of December 2026 as part of efforts to strike a balance between facilitating private sector investment and maintaining oversight of industrial land allocation.
Hashem said the first article of the new decree restructures the framework governing grace periods for delayed industrial projects based on their actual implementation rates.
Projects that have obtained building permits and completed at least 75% of construction will receive a maximum six-month extension, with full exemption from delay penalties, allowing them to complete construction, install machinery, and obtain operating and industrial licences after paying the applicable standard fees.
Projects that have completed between 50% and less than 75% of construction will be granted an extension of up to 12 months, with exemption from delay penalties during the first six months only. Standard penalties and fees will apply thereafter.
Projects that have completed less than 50% of construction, or have not started building despite obtaining the necessary permits, will receive a maximum 18-month extension, with exemption from delay penalties during the first six months and payment of the applicable penalties for the remaining period.
Meanwhile, projects that have already benefited from previous extensions but failed to demonstrate sufficient progress will receive a final three-month grace period. Failure to comply after that period will result in cancellation of the land allocation and the immediate withdrawal of the plot for reallocation.
The minister stressed that the new incentives will apply only to serious projects and will not cover industrial land where investors failed to demonstrate commitment and where formal cancellation or land withdrawal decisions have already been issued after the approved implementation timetable expired.
Under the second article of the decree, the government has also eased restrictions on industrial land transactions by removing the mandatory operating period previously required before transferring ownership or leasing industrial land.
Instead, beneficiaries holding land under sale, usufruct, or lease-to-own arrangements will be allowed to transfer ownership, assign their rights, or lease the land only after paying the full land price and all outstanding dues, obtaining operating and industrial licences, commencing actual production, and paying the applicable standard fees.
The decree also introduces greater flexibility for changing industrial activities.
Investors will now be permitted to shift from one industrial sector to another on allocated land within industrial zones and developer-operated industrial parks, subject to approval by the Industrial Development Authority. Approval will be based on a justified feasibility study, the suitability of the site’s location for the proposed activity, and payment of the required standard fees.

Italy declares nationwide red heat alert for major cities
Cities including Rome have introduced measures such as free access to air-conditioned cultural venues
Italy has placed all 27 of its major cities under the highest heat alert as the country's fourth heatwave of the summer pushes temperatures close to 40C.
The Italian Health Ministry said all cities monitored by its heat surveillance system will be under a red alert by Thursday, marking the first time this year that every monitored city has reached the highest warning level.
A red alert indicates an increased risk of health emergencies caused by prolonged extreme heat and applies to the entire population, not only vulnerable groups.
Authorities have advised people to avoid direct sunlight between 11:00 AM and 6:00 PM, remain indoors where possible, drink at least 1.5 litres of water daily, and avoid alcohol, coffee, fizzy drinks and heavy meals.
The heatwave has been linked to four recent deaths, including a 19-year-old tomato picker and a 40-year-old carpenter, while drought conditions continue to worsen across northern Italy.
The prolonged dry weather has also strained water supplies in more than 100 towns and affected agriculture, with lower crop yields and reduced milk production reported.
Atmospheric physicist Lorenzo Giovannini told Ansa news agency that this summer's heatwaves were already above average for both intensity and duration, adding that the climate crisis was making them "longer and more intense".
Cities including Rome have introduced measures such as free access to air-conditioned cultural venues and extended evening opening hours at major tourist sites.
